name: Questions to Ask a Los Angeles Driveway Contractor to Prevent Cracking

mainEntity.name: What should I ask a paving or driveway contractor in Los Angeles to ensure my new driveway won’t crack from tree roots or soil movement?
mainEntity.text: What should I ask a paving or driveway contractor in Los Angeles to ensure my new driveway won’t crack from tree roots or soil movement?

acceptedAnswer.text: Driveway failures in Los Angeles often stem from inadequate base preparation, tree roots, and poor drainage. When interviewing a paving or driveway contractor, ask them to explain their **subgrade preparation** in detail. They should plan for removal of unstable soils, proper compaction, and installation of a suitable gravel or road base layer of adequate thickness for your vehicle loads. Discuss **reinforcement** and control joints. Rebar or welded wire mesh and well-planned contraction joints help manage cracking. Ask where joints will be placed and how they will handle transitions to the garage slab or street. Tree roots are a major concern near driveways. Ask whether they use **root barriers**, how close they will pour to existing trees, and whether an arborist should be consulted for large, mature trees. Preventing water from pooling near roots and under the slab is equally important. Finally, confirm the **drainage plan**: slope direction, any trench or area drains, and how water will exit the property without eroding edges. Request a written description of base depth, reinforcement, mix design (for concrete), and warranty terms focused specifically on cracking and settlement.
acceptedAnswer.description: Ask about soil preparation, base thickness, reinforcement, root barriers, and drainage. A durable driveway design should include proper compaction, adequate gravel base, control joints, and strategies to manage roots and water so movement beneath the slab is minimized.
